questions.title: Timing of the fall event
questions.raisedNote: A guy asked how the nachash was in the garden if already evil. Recap left it open. Keep it open.
questions.notLocking: Do not lock a date. Do not pick option A or B as the house doctrine. Do not invent a Hollywood timeline that sequences Ezekiel 28, Genesis 3, and Job 1 into a movie. We hold the texts. The date is not a load-bearing call.
scriptureHold: Ezekiel 28:12-19 (and Isaiah 14 as the fall song): blameless from the day he was created until iniquity was found in him. Eden / holy mountain / guardian cherub language. Label the Tyre stacking as already taught: the text starts with a human prince and then describes a being beyond that king. Do not flatten the oracle into only Tyre. Do not skip the human prince either.

Genesis 3: the nachash is in the garden, crafty, speaking. New cherubim and a flaming sword in 3:24 AFTER the nachash is no longer guardian. That last call is SETTLED. Do not re-correct it. Week 1 already taught it. If you reopen “was the nachash still the gate-cherub after the exile,” you are walking backward.

Job 1:6 and 2:1: the adversary is among the sons of God presenting themselves before Yahweh. Access to the court after Eden is already in the book. Do not flatten “God cannot be near sin” into a reason the scene is impossible. The book already put him there. Yahweh remains God. Permission is not absence.
options: A) Already fallen before the garden temptation. God still allowed the test. That is the Job pattern: the adversary is already the adversary when he presents himself, and Yahweh still permits a proving.

B) The garden is the moment iniquity is found. He was still in the guardian post until then. Ezekiel’s “until iniquity was found” lands in Genesis 3, and 3:24 is the new guard after that post is empty.
questions.tension: If already fallen, why still the guardian in Eden? If the garden is the fall, Job 1 still shows him in the court later. We hold both texts. We do not invent a Hollywood timeline to make the tension go away.
notes: Both options stay on the table. Status is open. If they ask tonight, name the tension and the three texts. Do not close it for them. Recap left it open on purpose.

Extra-biblical: 1 Enoch’s third of the stars, and Enoch’s 200 Watchers, stay labeled EXTRA_BIBLICAL. Those are a DIFFERENT event from the Eden rebel, and a DIFFERENT event from Genesis 6 sons of God. Do not mash Lucifer’s fall with the Genesis 6 sons of God. Do not mash Enoch’s rebel class-word with Daniel 4’s holy Watcher. Genesis 6 is Week 2. The nachash is Week 1. Keep the ranks unmashed.

If you mention this in the room, say out loud that the date is not locked. Then land on what is locked: 3:24 new cherubim after the nachash is no longer guardian; Job 1 the adversary is in the court; Ezekiel 28 iniquity was found after he was created blameless. Do not send this card in GroupMe.

questions.title: Acts 21 — why Paul takes the vow and offering
questions.firstRaised: Seaver’s own sincere question (Granola creation chat / study file). Candidate from teacher prep. Not a class dump.
questions.raisedNote: This is a teacher-prep card. Do not send it in GroupMe. Do not put it on the guys’ page. If it never comes up in the room, leave it here.
questions.notLocking: Do not lock a motive. “He was trying to please men” and “God beat him for it” are working hunches, not the tracker’s verdict. Status is open. Do not preach either hunch as settled.
scriptureHold: Acts 21:17-26. Paul arrives in Jerusalem. James and the elders hear what God has done among the Gentiles. They name a rumor: 21:21, that Paul teaches Jews among the nations to abandon Moses — not to circumcise sons, not to walk the customs. They propose: four men under a vow; purify yourself with them; pay their expenses; so they may shave their heads; then all will know the rumor is nothing and you yourself walk keeping the law. An offering is presented for each of them. The text says he did it.

Galatians 2, including the Antioch clash with Peter, is the earlier preaching they hear as tension. Paul has already stood up when table-fellowship with Gentiles was being walked back. That is why Acts 21 feels like a problem, not a footnote. Hold both. Do not cut Galatians to make Acts smooth. Do not cut Acts to make Galatians the only Paul.

Acts 21:27ff: the riot follows in the temple. Jews from Asia see him, seize him, charge that he teaches against the people, the law, and this place, and that he brought Greeks into the temple. The vow-and-offering did not quiet the rumor. Name that. Do not turn the riot into a tidy moral of the story unless the text says so.
options: Working hunch, not locked: he was trying to please men — James, the elders, the Jerusalem rumormongers — and the vow is accommodation.
Working hunch, not locked: God beat him for it; the riot is discipline for walking back into a vow-and-offering he had already relativized for the nations.
questions.tension: The text says he did it. The tension with his own gospel to the Gentiles is real. Do not use this to throw Paul out. Do not sand the tension away. Do not lock a motive.
notes: Hold: he did take the purification and pay the expenses and present the offering. Luke wrote it. We do not get to un-happen it because it is awkward next to Galatians.

Do not use Acts 21 to un-gospel Paul, to dump him as a false apostle, or to baptize Torah-for-Gentiles through the back door. Do not use Galatians to pretend Acts 21 is a smear Luke should have cut. Both books are Scripture.

If it comes up in the room, name the rumor (21:21), name what he did (21:23-26), name the riot (21:27ff), name Galatians 2 as the earlier clash they already know as tension. Then stop. Motive stays open. Do not send this card in GroupMe.
